study_identification.author_journal_year: Kasper et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2024
study_identification.title: Resting-State Changes in Aging and Parkinson's Disease Are Shaped by Underlying Neurotransmission: A Normative Modeling Study

study_characteristics.study_objective: To test whether and how age- and Parkinson's disease-related resting-state changes in commonly applied local and global activity and connectivity measures colocalize with underlying neurotransmitter systems using normative modeling and in vivo maps for various neurochemical systems in the UK Biobank cohort.

hc_age.answer: mean 64.03; sd 7.5; min 44.58; max 81.98 (overall); Females: mean 63.5, sd 7.4; Males: mean 64.7, sd 7.6

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: UK Biobank initial preprocessing (T1 quality control, gradient distortion correction, motion correction, grand-mean intensity normalization, high-pass temporal filtering, EPI unwarping, ICA+FIX for artifact removal); SPM12; FSL v5.0; CONN toolbox (MATLAB v2020b); MNI space normalization; resampling (3mm³ isotropic); smoothing (Gaussian kernel 4mm FWHM); bandpass filtering (0.008-0.09 Hz); 24-parameter motion regression; white matter and CSF signal regression; Neuromorphometrics atlas (119 regions) for regional analyses

quality_checking_detail.answer: Distorted images and artifacts identified by low correlations (r < 0.9) between individual and reference preprocessed mean rs-fMRI image of 200 subjects. Visual inspection confirmed failed spatial normalization or insufficient brain coverage. Excluded data from subjects with excessive in-scanner motion (maximum frame-wise rotation > 2° and movement > 3 mm). First five frames discarded to ensure signal equilibrium.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Single-site study (UK Biobank). No multi-site harmonization required.

modeling_method.answer: Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with 5 knot basis splines and sinh-arcsinh warping

response_variable.answer: Colocalization strength (Fisher's z-transformed Spearman correlation coefficients) between individual brain functional measures (fALFF, LCOR, GCOR) and neurotransmitter systems (19 PET-derived neurotransmitter maps)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex modeled as covariates in Bayesian linear regression framework to account for non-linear trajectories and non-Gaussian variance of normal colocalization levels.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study explicitly addresses nuisance structure in multiple ways: (1) Quality control procedures remove distorted images and excessive motion data; (2) 24-parameter motion regression explicitly handles motion artifacts; (3) White matter and CSF signals are regressed out; (4) The normative model uses sinh-arcsinh warping to account for non-Gaussian variance (heteroscedasticity), which directly addresses variance differences across age; (5) The study explicitly tests for and identifies nonconstant variance (heteroscedasticity) using White test and Goldfeld-Quandt test; (6) Atrophy correction is performed by regressing out gray matter volume effects voxel-wise; (7) Sex is included as a covariate in the model. The paper demonstrates thorough handling of mean shifts (motion, WM/CSF signals), variance differences (heteroscedasticity across age), and nonlinearity (basis splines).
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We applied a bandpass filter (0.008 - 0.09 Hz) to the BOLD signal, discarded the first five frames to ensure signal equilibrium, and regressed out 24 parameters of motion, as well as the mean signal from white matter and cerebrospinal fluid using CONN... We additionally excluded data from subjects with excessive in-scanner motion (maximum frame-wise rotation > 2° and movement > 3 mm)... To account for non-linear trajectories and non-Gaussian variance of the normal co-localization levels, we used Bayesian linear regression (5 knot basis splines and sinh-arcsinh warping) with age and sex as covariates... Using the White test, we first identified all pairs of brain function measures and PET maps whose correlation coefficients exhibited nonconstant variance across age... To control for aging-related atrophy, we generated normalized and smoothed grey matter volumes... Next, the linear effects of grey matter signals from all fALFF, LCOR, and GCOR maps were regressed voxel-wise.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Supplementary Methods lines 11-12, 29; Main text Methods section; Results section on heteroscedasticity

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study reports various model evaluation metrics implicitly through the analysis of colocalization patterns. While the paper reports correlation coefficients, statistical significance testing, and variance analyses for the healthy cohort, it does not explicitly report standard normative modeling validation metrics (e.g., MSLL, EV, skewness, kurtosis of z-scores) on held-out healthy control data or using cross-validation within the training dataset. The focus is on applying the model to PD patients rather than validating model performance on held-out healthy controls.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The study presents extensive statistical analyses of colocalization patterns including Spearman correlation coefficients, significance testing (p-values with FDR correction), variance analyses (White test, Goldfeld-Quandt test), and regional contribution analyses. However, explicit normative model validation metrics like MSLL, EV, or distributional properties of z-scores in held-out healthy samples are not reported.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not report validation of the normative model on an independent healthy control dataset from the same domain (UK Biobank or similar population-based neuroimaging cohort). All healthy controls from UK Biobank (n=25,917) appear to be used for model training, and the model is directly applied to PD patients for deviation scoring. No mention of external validation on independent healthy samples is provided.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: We included 25,917 adult participants from the UK Biobank not diagnosed with psychiatric, cognitive, or neurological disorders... as a control cohort. We also identified a group of 58 participants from the UK Biobank who were diagnosed with idiopathic PD... Normative modeling of colocalizations between brain function and neurotransmitter systems was based on the data of HCs.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not validate the normative model on data from a different domain (e.g., different cohort, scanner, protocol, or population). The model is trained on UK Biobank healthy controls and applied only to UK Biobank PD patients, which represents the same imaging protocol and population sampling frame. No external validation cohorts from different sources are mentioned.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The entire analysis is conducted within the UK Biobank cohort: healthy controls (n=25,917) for normative modeling and PD patients (n=58) for deviation analysis. No mention of external cohorts or cross-domain validation.

deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores from normative models of colocalization strength (Fisher's z-transformed Spearman correlation coefficients between functional measures and neurotransmitter maps); deviation assessed via t-tests comparing PD group z-scores to null distribution; regional contribution quantified via leave-one-region-out Δρ² analysis

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: One-sample t-tests (alpha=0.05) to test whether PD deviation scores were significantly different from null distribution; Pearson correlations between deviation scores and disease duration; Pearson correlations between deviation scores and cognitive scores; Regional analyses: leave-one-region-out approach to quantify regional contribution (Δρ²) to observed deviations; Pearson correlations between regional contribution maps (Δρ²) and regional effect sizes (Cohen's d) for functional differences (fALFF, LCOR, GCOR) between PD and age-/sex-matched HC subgroup (n=17,400); Mann-Whitney-U tests for identifying regions with significant functional differences between PD and matched controls; FDR and Bonferroni-Holm corrections for multiple comparisons
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Age-related changes in resting-state functional measures (fALFF, LCOR, GCOR) colocalized with multiple major neurotransmitter systems (serotonergic, dopaminergic, noradrenergic, glutamatergic); PD patients showed significant deviations from normative colocalization patterns across various neurotransmitter systems; deviation in LCOR-GABAA colocalization correlated with disease duration (Pearson's r = -0.38, pFDR = 0.027).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: In healthy aging (n=25,917, age 64.03±7.5 years), widespread age-related decreases in fALFF, LCOR, and GCOR were observed in most cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions. Group-level aging effects colocalized significantly (pFDR<0.05) with serotonergic, dopaminergic, noradrenergic (also GCOR), and glutamatergic neurotransmission for fALFF and LCOR. At the individual level, colocalization strengths changed with age, explaining up to 3%, 4%, and 1% of variance for fALFF (with NMDA and SERT), LCOR (with SERT), and GCOR (with VAChT), respectively. Variance in colocalization patterns increased with age for multiple neurotransmitter systems: higher variability in older vs. younger subpopulation was found for 11 of 14 neurotransmitter systems for fALFF, 14 of 15 for LCOR, and 7 of 11 for GCOR (Goldfeld-Quandt test, pFDR<0.05). In PD patients (n=58, age 68.6±6.5 years, disease duration variable), significant deviations from normative colocalization patterns were found: for fALFF, lower colocalization with serotonergic, GABAergic, muscarinic, and glutamatergic systems; for LCOR and GCOR, lower colocalizations with serotonergic, dopaminergic, GABAergic, histaminergic, noradrenergic, glutamatergic, and cholinergic systems. Notably, the deviation in LCOR-GABAA colocalization was negatively correlated with disease duration (Pearson's r = -0.38, pFDR = 0.027), suggesting progressive GABAergic pathology. No significant correlations were found between colocalization deviations and cognitive scores. Regional contribution analyses revealed that basal ganglia, insula, occipital regions (fALFF), and additionally subcallosal areas, thalamus, basal forebrain, pre-/postcentral regions (LCOR/GCOR) contributed most to PD-related colocalization alterations. Regional contributions for glutamatergic system deviations were significantly correlated with regional functional alterations in PD (pFDR<0.05). Most findings remained significant after atrophy correction, except LCOR-5-HT1B and LCOR-VAChT associations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study cohort was recruited as a representative sample of healthy UK residents, which may introduce biases including high average socioeconomic status and low alcohol/tobacco consumption, potentially limiting generalizability to broader populations. Participants with mild depressive symptoms (12.32% with ICD-10: F32) were included to avoid cohort bias, given 11% prevalence in UK population, but this may affect interpretation of 'healthy' aging patterns. PD severity assessment was limited: no standardized PD severity scores (e.g., UPDRS or Hoehn & Yahr stages) were available; disease duration was used as a proxy for severity but is a crude approximation. PD medication effects on functional measures were not controlled, though previous work (reference 25) suggests medication effects on spatial colocalization are negligible compared to disease effects. Limited cognitive score availability restricted analysis of cognition-deviation associations. PET maps were derived from differently aged healthy populations, potentially introducing bias as receptor/transporter distributions may change during aging. The normative model was not validated on independent healthy cohorts or cross-domain datasets, limiting assessment of model generalizability and robustness. Sample size for PD group was relatively small (n=58), which may limit statistical power for subgroup analyses and correlation analyses with clinical variables. Cross-sectional design limits inference about longitudinal trajectories and causal relationships between neurotransmitter changes and functional alterations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates the feasibility of combining normative modeling with neurotransmitter mapping to understand neurophysiological mechanisms underlying age- and disease-related functional brain changes. The approach may aid future research and drug development through deeper understanding of specific neurotransmitter systems' vulnerability in aging and neurological diseases. The finding of GABAergic system involvement in PD progression (correlation with disease duration) suggests potential for novel drug targets and monitoring strategies. The increased variance in colocalization patterns in older individuals may reflect undetected neurodegenerative processes in cognitively normal older populations, given high prevalence of neuropathology in this group. The distinct colocalization patterns of various neurotransmitter systems with functional changes in aging vs. PD point to distinct pathophysiological processes. The method allows for individual-level characterization of deviations from normative aging trajectories, potentially enabling precision medicine approaches. Further validation with clinical severity scores and larger patient samples with diverse neurological conditions is needed to establish clinical utility.

general_notes.general_notes: This study represents a methodologically innovative approach by combining normative modeling of functional neuroimaging measures with spatial colocalization analysis using PET-derived neurotransmitter maps. The normative model was applied to colocalization patterns (correlation coefficients) rather than raw neuroimaging features, which is a novel analytical framework. The study used 19 distinct neurotransmitter maps from independent PET/SPECT studies covering major neurotransmitter systems: serotonergic (5-HT1A, 5-HT1B, 5-HT2A, 5-HT4, 5-HT6, SERT), dopaminergic (D1, D2, DAT), cholinergic (M1, α4β2, VAChT), glutamatergic (mGluR5, NMDA), GABAergic (GABAA), and others (histamine H3, norepinephrine transporter, cannabinoid CB1, μ-opioid). Source publications and sample characteristics for each PET map are provided in Supplementary Table 2. The study explicitly tested for heteroscedasticity (nonconstant variance) across age using White test and Goldfeld-Quandt test, representing rigorous handling of nuisance structure. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses were performed with atrophy correction by regressing out voxelwise gray matter volumes. The Neuromorphometrics atlas with 119 regions was used for spatial colocalization analyses; previous work by authors (reference 51) showed atlas choice with comparable number of parcels has negligible effect on colocalization patterns. Three complementary functional measures were analyzed: fALFF (fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations, 0.008-0.09 Hz, power ratio measure of local activity), LCOR (local correlation, Gaussian kernel 25mm FWHM, local synchronicity measure), and GCOR (global correlation, global synchronicity measure without distance-weighting). For PD patients, disease duration was computed as difference between date of first ICD-10 G20 diagnosis (Data-Field 131022) and imaging date (Data-Field 53, Instance 2). An age- and sex-matched HC subgroup (n=17,400) was used for regional comparison analyses in PD. Total pool was 30,035 participants; after exclusions based on diseases with known brain effects, 25,917 HCs remained for normative modeling; 3 additional participants were excluded from atrophy-corrected analyses due to missing structural data (n=25,914). Exclusion criteria for HC group are detailed in Supplementary Table 1 (ICD-10 codes: F01-F03, F10-F19, F20-F22, F25, F31, F33, F70-F72, G04-G07, G10-G14, G20-G25, G30-G37, G40-G41, G45, C71). The study received ethics approval and UK Biobank Resource Application Number 41655.
